Paradox

/PAIR-uh-doks/ - the stress falls on PAIR · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Paradox means an apparently contradictory statement that may be true.

Grandpa swore by the farmhouse paradox: crack a window in January and the old stove will heat the room faster.

Worked Example

The safety office wrestles with a stubborn paradox: the better the new harnesses became, the more falls the site recorded, as crews inched out onto beams they once refused to walk.

A paradox is not a mistake — it's a statement or situation that contradicts itself on the surface yet proves true underneath, which is why a paradox repays a second look instead of a correction.

How Paradox Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

contradiction

contradiction: two claims that cannot both be true — with no rescue coming

enigma

enigma: a mystery that invites decoding

Antonyms

truism

truism: a statement so obviously true it teaches nothing

commonplace

commonplace: an ordinary remark nobody blinks at

How Strong Is It? — oddity → paradox → absurdity

oddity vs. paradox

oddity vs. paradox: An oddity is milder than a paradox — merely strange, with no real contradiction inside it.

absurdity vs. paradox

absurdity vs. paradox: Absurdity goes further than paradox: a paradox contradicts itself yet may be true, while an absurdity collapses under its own nonsense.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of paradox.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — para-

Prefix — para-: beside, beyond

Root — dox

Root — dox: opinion, belief (Greek doxa)

Put it together

Put it together: Para- (beside, beyond) + dox (opinion, belief) = beside received opinion. A paradox stands just outside what everyone believes — and turns out, on inspection, to be holding its ground.

Use the root in a new word: paralegal

Use the root in a new word: paralegal: The paralegal worked beside the lead attorney all night, flagging exhibits for the morning.

Root Check

Word Choice

neutral / academic

Paradox is for claims and situations that contradict themselves yet hold — use it precisely, not for every oddity or coincidence. Its unit-mate conundrum wants solving; a paradox mostly wants understanding.
